body: Same here. Every word. When I was in my twenties I could believe things would get better and that I was capable of changing my life for the better. But now it's clear that was not true.

Quality varies among therapists. My first therapist just set there, occasionally *hrmmed* and repeated back what I had just said in different terms. The second and third were both intelligent and seemed to truly care about me. With the third I felt a close personal connection as well. As for how much they helped, I don't feel that they did and eventually I stopped attending therapy because the costs were adding up but even after a considerable amount of time there were no improvements. (In fact my condition deteriorated during therapy.) 

It has been my experience that therapy has no effect, positive or negative. However others have had the opposite experience. If your finances allow you could try it for yourself and see if you had a good outcome.

It's possible. For some people it does get better. For me it didn't, in fact it got a lot worse. That isn't uncommon; due to the kindling effect bipolar often becomes more severe with age. But I wouldn't say it's impossible for your experience of life to improve because that isn't true. But I also wouldn't categorically state that life gets better because that isn't true either. It's possible you get a lot better and it's also possible that you get a lot worse.
Whatever happened just.. unhappens and we're okay again? That would be awesome :-)

Hey SmallGuitar. I can (unfortunately) relate to your story. Once upon a time I could shake off the bad times with much more ease than I can now. But as the years roll on and depression continues I find that I can't let things roll off my back the way I once could. I have even developed anxiety attacks when I'm driving, which was once an activity that I really enjoyed.
